title: Engrams act more like prompts decoded by an intelligent receiver than like encodings

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Engrams act more like prompts decoded by an intelligent receiver than like encodings

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: From examples such as frogs that seek out an odorant injected into the egg they developed from, Levin argues that engrams behave less like encoded memories and more like prompts, with much of the work (detecting novelty, remapping across scales, contextualizing and generalizing) done by the encoding and decoding process.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2024, Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue › 3. Remapping Memories: Beyond Storage and Simple Modification

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The engrams seem less like encoded memories29, and more like a kind of prompt, with a lot of the hard work being carried out through the encoding/decoding process, which adds interpretation, context sensitivity, and generalization (i.e., intelligence) to the process.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue”, Entropy (Basel, Switzerland) (2024), doi:10.3390/e26060481; section “3. Remapping Memories: Beyond Storage and Simple Modification”. Scope: Memory transfer phenomena in animals (frog eggs, Aplysia brain-extract transfer)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2024-memory-06: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.34

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Some component phenomena are behaviourally measurable, but the central prompt metaphor admits multiple operationalizations. Public data are sparse and even positive transfer results do not sharply distinguish the proposed interpretation from ordinary associative mechanisms.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure whether transferred or embryonically introduced memory-associated material supports context-sensitive generalization that cannot be predicted from a fixed one-to-one code. Flexible transfer across locations or contexts supports a prompt-like account; invariant, location-specific decoding supports a fixed-encoding rival.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Successful generalization does not uniquely imply intelligent decoding.

Several cited phenomena are old or disputed.

Prompt versus encoding is not a standard quantitative contrast.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.55
data adequacy: 0.25
discriminating power: 0.25
operationalizability: 0.35
data existence: 0.35

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim is that engrams are better understood as prompts, with intelligence located in encoding and decoding. Specificity, generalization, and context dependence are expected on both that reading and a standard encoding-plus-retrieval reading. No existing measurement separates the two, so the contrast is not empirically resolvable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Transfer and odor-seeking experiments can show that a stored trace is incomplete without later interpretation, but both a prompt model and an encoding model predict context-sensitive readout.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Prompt versus engram is a description of the same encode-and-decode process.

The cited frog and Aplysia transfer cases do not uniquely favor one description.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.2
data existence: 0.2
operationalizability: 0.3
data adequacy: 0.15
discriminating power: 0.15
